messages:
alice_customer: Hey team — after migrating svc-api.mycorp.internal to a new Route53 private hosted zone, our ECS tasks inside the customer VPC get NXDOMAIN for svc-api.mycorp.internal. Public prod is fine. Any ideas?

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste output of `dig +short svc-api.mycorp.internal @10.0.0.2` from a failing instance and `ip route`?

alice_customer: dig output:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc-api.mycorp.internal @10.0.0.2
;; global options: +cmd
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
``` 
Also traceroute to 10.0.0.2 times out.

kai_oncall: Does the VPC have the new zone associated? Sometimes duplicate private hosted zones cause which zone answers to be unpredictable.

devon_platform: Can you run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name mycorp.internal` and check for multiple private zones in the account/region? Also check cross-account private zones.

alice_customer: Ran list-hosted-zones-by-name — I see two hosted zones with the same name, one created yesterday in account A (new migration) and one older in account B. Both are private.

maria_support: Bingo. Route 53 resolution for private hosted zones depends on VPC associations. If there are overlapping private zones (even across accounts) you can get flapping or NXDOMAIN depending on association order.

devon_platform: Troubleshooting steps: 1) Verify VPC associations for both zones: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z123...` 2) Check `vpc` blocks in the hosted-zone details to see which VPCs are associated. 3) If both zones are associated with the same VPC (via cross-account association), decide which to keep. 4) Remove the VPC association from the stale zone or delete the stale hosted zone. 5) Flush instance DNS cache (`sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` or `sudo service nscd restart`) and retest.

alice_customer: Confirmed the old zone is still associated via cross-account association. Removing that association now.

route53-bot: Hosted zone association removed (zone ZAAA -> vpc-0abcde) by alice_customer

alice_customer: After removing the association `dig +short svc-api.mycorp.internal @10.0.0.2` now returns `10.10.5.20` from inside the VPC and service is responding.

maria_support: Great — follow-up suggestions: export zone contents, delete the stale hosted zone to avoid accidental reassociation, and add migration notes. Also check for any resolver rules that might forward the internal name elsewhere.

kai_oncall: I'll add a short playbook to eng-runbooks called "private hosted zone migration checklist" with the validation commands and common gotchas.

alice_customer: One more Q: we also have a public svc-api.mycorp.com that points to other infra. Any gotchas mixing public and private records under similar names?

devon_platform: Public and private hosted zones are separate in Route 53. The only gotcha is if you reuse the exact same domain name and accidentally create overlapping private zones across accounts. If you need split-horizon with the same apex, prefer a controlled single private zone and use conditional forwarding only when necessary. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Closing the thread — please reopen if anything else shows up. :white_check_mark:
